evidence_quotes: Nikolski, Alaska dominated the activity, accounting for 13 of 16 events (81%)
shallow follow-on sequence east of Nikolski (depths as low as 1.0–5.8 km)
Watch closely for: continued shallow seismicity east of Nikolski, any event exceeding M6.5 in this cluster
The M6.2 event near Nikolski on January 25 is the standout signal
criticisms: No explicit 24-hour action items are provided — the report never tells a coordinator to 'alert Aleutians Islands Borough emergency management', 'request USGS aftershock probability assessment for Nikolski', or 'verify shelter/infrastructure status in Nikolski'. The watch items are monitoring-oriented but not decision-grade.

No resource pre-positioning guidance: given 81% of events cluster near Nikolski and several are extremely shallow, the report should recommend whether to pre-position search-and-rescue assets or conduct welfare checks on the small Nikolski community.
The tsunami risk framing is reassuring but passive — no recommendation to verify PTWC notification protocols or confirm local warning system readiness in the Aleutian chain.

The 'building sequence vs. tapering aftershocks' question is raised but left unresolved with no guidance on what threshold would trigger escalation (e.g., 'if a M5.5+ occurs within 50 km of Nikolski in the next 7 days, escalate to full advisory').
No mention of population exposure or infrastructure at risk in Nikolski, which would help coordinators calibrate response urgency.
